paragraphs.text: Praemonstrante et instruente eum Eli. Eli being his tutor and teacher, he was tractable and officious, faithful in a little, and therefore intrusted with more, being the next famous prophet to Moses, and called the first. {Act 3:24 2Ch 35:18}
paragraphs.anchor: And the child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Rare. The Hebrews put rarum pro charo: as Pro 25:17, "Let thy feet be precious in thy neighbour’s house," that is, let them seldom come there. See Psa 74:9 Isa 13:12. A prophet was a rare bird; so was once a preacher in this land, and then much more set by. Diaconos paucitas honorabiles fecit. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: The word of the Lord was precious in those days.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Broken. See Jdg 7:15, with the note. Prophecy was very scarce.
paragraphs.anchor: There was no open vision.

paragraphs.text: {a} Jer., Epist.
Much about that time that the aforesaid prophet had spoken to Eli, {1Sa 2:27-36} or not long after. Clouds cluster against a storm. Or rather, At that time when the word of God was precious.
paragraphs.anchor: At that time.

paragraphs.text: Tηλαυγες, clearly, and far off. The Rabbins interpret it of the eyes of his mind also, as that he had lost the gift of prophecy: and do therefore note a special providence, that when one light failed, God set up another, viz., Samuel.
paragraphs.anchor: That he could not see.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Early in the morning, before it was day. For they did not then burn daylight, as the superstitious Papists do by their tapers burning upon their altars at noonday. The morning is the fittest time for meditation and prayer.
paragraphs.anchor: And ere the lamp of God went out

paragraphs.text: In some of the Levites’ lodgings, and not far from Eli, on whom he waited.
paragraphs.anchor: And Samuel was laid down to sleep.

paragraphs.text: Gratuita et inopinata est vocatio nostra {Eph 1:11} God calleth his people of free grace, and when they least think of it.
paragraphs.anchor: That the Lord called Samuel

paragraphs.text: A hearing ear is a sweet mercy: a heavy ear, a grievous judgment. {Isa 6:9}
paragraphs.anchor: And he answered, Here am I.

paragraphs.text: This showeth his diligence in attending on his blind master, though he were now but twelve years old, as saith Josephus.
paragraphs.anchor: And he ran unto Eli.

paragraphs.text: sc., To sleep; which he would not have done had he thought that the Lord had spoken to him. So if men did but consider that it is God that speaketh unto them by the mouth of his ministers, they would hear and heed much better.
paragraphs.anchor: And he went and lay down

paragraphs.text: How oft do we either turn the deaf ear to God’s call, or else mistake, and run another way, till he please to speak home to our hearts, and "cause us to hear him," as the Church speaks! {Son 8:13}
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord called yet again, Samuel.

paragraphs.text: i.e., He knew him not in that way peculiar to prophets: for otherwise he knew the Lord a far deal better than Eli’s two sons did, {1Sa 2:12} and yet he and they had all one tutor. But he hath his chair in heaven who teacheth the heart, saith a father.
paragraphs.anchor: Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord

paragraphs.text: There was a special providence in it, that Samuel should thus run to Eli three several times, that he might surely know it to be a divine revelation, and be affected with it. Whereas else he might have slighted it as a childish dream; or have thought it strange that God should use the pupil to instruct the tutor. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child.

paragraphs.text: {a} P. Martyr.

Eli, though his conscience told him that Samuel would shortly bespeak him, as afterwards Ahijah the prophet did Jeroboam’s wife, "I am sent to thee with heavy tidings," {1Ki 14:6} yet he instructeth him when God called again, what answer he should make: and saith in effect, as that holy Dutch doctor did, Veniat, veniat verbum Dei et submittemus ei, sexcenta si nobis essent colla. Let the word of God be what it will, I will surely submit to it.
paragraphs.anchor: That thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth.

paragraphs.text: In some visible shape, either by an angel, or at least as he did, late in Queen Mary’s days, to Robert Samuel, martyr, who having been long kept in close prison by the Bishop of Norwich without food and drink, saving that he had every day allowed him two or three morsels of bread and three spoonfuls of water, to the end he might be reserved to further torment, he fell one time into a sleep, as it were one half in a slumber: at which time one clad all in white seemed to stand before him, which ministered comfort unto him by these words - Samuel, Samuel, be of good cheer, and take a good heart unto thee, for after this day thou shalt never be either hungry or thirsty.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord came, and stood.

paragraphs.text: For speedily after he was burned, and from that time till he should suffer, he felt neither hunger nor thirst. And this declared he, as he said, that all men might behold the wonderful works of God. {a} The like befell Cuthbert Simson, martyr. {b}
{a} Act. and Mon., fol. 1547.
{b} Ibid., fol. 1844.

All the people are threatened, as well us those priests; because for their faults they abhorred the Lord’s sacrifice, and from the priests "profaneness was gone forth into all the land," {Jer 23:15} so that there was "like priest, like people."
paragraphs.anchor: I will do a thing in Israel.

paragraphs.text: Through horror and amazement, as useth to fall out upon some sudden thunder clap, or the roaring of great ordnance, or the fall of those huge heaps of snow in the Alps, called by the inhabitants Labinae. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: At which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lavat., in Judic., pp. 18,31. Vatab.

Praestabo reipsa quod verbis minitor. Execution of justice is God’s work, though his strange work, {Isa 28:21} and when be once beginneth, he will go thorough stitch with it: he will neither dally nor desist till it be done.
paragraphs.anchor: When I begin, I will also make an end.

paragraphs.text: And he shall find that I told him so not in terrorem, only to frighten him.
paragraphs.anchor: For I have told him.

paragraphs.text: Both by that prophet, {1Sa 2:29} and by that domestical chaplain, his conscience.
paragraphs.anchor: For the iniquity which he knoweth.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Contemned or despised themselves - viz., by despising their ways, not ordering them aright {Pro 19:16} - and so have rendered themselves contemptible, or accursed, and the service of God also, by their maladministration: for who will taste of the fruit that first disliketh the tree?
paragraphs.anchor: Because his sons made themselves vile.

paragraphs.text: No, not so much as by frowning upon them - so the word signifieth - by casting a wry look toward them. A Christian should carry a severe rebuke in his countenance at least, as God doth. {Psa 80:16}
paragraphs.anchor: And he restrained them not.

paragraphs.text: That the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged.] Hence some concluded that their sin was that sin unto death, {1Jn 5:16} for which "there remaineth no more sacrifice," {Heb 10:26} and that they were damned, because so hardened that they could not repent. {Rom 1:28} If some of that race proved right, as they did, yet the temporal punishment of losing the chief priesthood could not be averted or avoided.

And Samuel … opened the doors of the house.] His modesty appeareth in that, (1.) He doeth his former office of doorkeeper, though he were now become a prophet: he was not at all puffed up with his new honour; (2.) He is not forward, but fearful to tell Eli the oracle, which yet he might not conceal.
He had a sore conscience, as his sons a seared, and such as presaged no good.
paragraphs.anchor: Then Eli called Samuel.

paragraphs.text: He is earnest to know the worst: for any good from an offended God he expected not. But "do not my words do good to him that walketh uprightly?" {Mic 2:7} {See Trapp on "Mic 2:7"}
paragraphs.anchor: What is the thing that the Lord, &c.

paragraphs.text: Bitter truths must be spoken, however they be taken; and if ministers be mannerly in the form, yet in the matter of their message let them be resolute.
paragraphs.anchor: Told him every whit.

paragraphs.text: Jehovah the Essentiator and the Promise keeper.
paragraphs.anchor: It is the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Let him do, {a} &c.] His holy will be done. This he speaketh not out of pervicacy or hypocrisy, as some have censured, but in a humble submission to his heavenly Father: for if Eli had been an ill father to his sons, yet he was a good son to God.
{a} Faciat quod vult, non discedo: Et si perire me volet, ipse perdat me, dum ego serve illi. - Tertul.
Metaph. a liquidis, aut ab aedificationibus collapsis.
paragraphs.anchor: Fall to the ground.

paragraphs.text: Because his words were fulfilled.
paragraphs.anchor: That Samuel was established.

paragraphs.text: That is, By Christ, {as 2Sa 7:21} or by prophetic revelation.
paragraphs.anchor: By the word of the Lord.
